objective: The rail's selection is a mark that travels — the same law as the list's carrier, and the same porteur.

the_law.one_marker_two_surfaces: SelectionMarker and advance_marker left views/package_workstation.rs and now live in state/motion.rs, beside carrier_travel. The rail and the list do not know each other; they know a row, the row it came from, and the number of the voyage. The four tests that prove the marker moved with it, names unchanged.
the_law.the_rail_is_equal_rows: The rail's entries have one height (38 px), one gap (2 px) and one top pad (8 px), named in UiMetrics. The mark's position is therefore a multiplication — rail_mark_top(index) — not a measurement of the layout, which is what lets an absolutely positioned 2 px bar sit exactly on the entry a row would occupy.
the_law.the_mark: a 2 px accent bar, drawn after the rows, at the row's left edge (x = 6, where the entry's border used to be). The entry keeps its fill and its accent label; the border_l_2 that used to be the selection is gone.

the_curve.what_changed: the rail's travel and the carrier's travel now take Curve::IN_OUT. They took Curve::OUT.
the_curve.why: the out curve is front-loaded: at a tenth of the time it has covered about half the distance. A mark sent along it arrives before the eye has left the row it departed — it reads as a jump with a tail. A travel leaves a place and arrives at another; both ends are watched. The out curve belongs to entries, where the element has no place to leave.
the_curve.the_frames: with the out curve, the rail's mark crossed four rows in ~2 captured frames (29 ms apart) and the rest of the 220 ms was a sub-pixel crawl. With the aller-retour the same four rows are crossed in 8–9 frames, symmetric: 71 → 75 → 121 → 182 → 225 → 231 (60 px strip, x = 6, window y), and 71 → 80 → 93 → 113 → 141 → 174 → 203 → 222 → 229 → 231 on a faster capture. The carrier, six rows apart: 327 → 338 → 353 → 376 → 407 → 444 → 476 → 497 → 505 → 507 (window y, x = 192).

what_was_seen.the_rail: the bar sits exactly on the selected entry: at rest it spans the entry's full height, 2 px wide, at the same x the border occupied (111..148 against a fill of 111..148).
what_was_seen.the_destination: the fill moves at once to the chosen entry; only the bar travels. That is the point: the fill is the row's state, the bar is the selection's place, and one of them is a fact the instant you click.
what_was_seen.the_keyboard: unchanged; the entries are still focusable and tab_stop, and the mark does not depend on focus.
what_was_seen.reduce_motion: the bar is rendered at its destination without an animation element, like the needle and the carrier.

the_artefacts.what: SelectionMarker and advance_marker joined the motion vocabulary, with their four tests
the rail's rows are one height, the selection is a 2 px mark that travels, and rail_mark_top is tested
the rail's marker is advanced where the rail's selection is read
the carrier takes the aller-retour; the definitions moved out
the rail's mark row, the curve law, and the focus-ring gap
six frames of the travel: 0 ms, ~50, ~120, ~180, ~230, landed

the_environment.the_click: a rail click needs cursor move → ~0.6 s → press (0x40) → ~0.12 s → release (0x80). Shorter settle times and a 0.05 s press gap produced dropped clicks in three separate runs: the app simply never saw the press. The frames that first 'proved' the mark was static were frames of a click that never happened.
the_environment.the_capture: grim on a 60 × 340 region takes ~29 ms; on 200 × 340 about 50 ms. A 220 ms travel is therefore 4–8 frames, and the burst must be started before the click — the click's own latency is longer than the animation.
